content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should it make easier or better for you than your current way of saving bookmarks?

Honestly, right now my bookmarks are a mess — they're scattered across my browser in folders, and once I've saved a few hundred I can never find the one I'm looking for again. So the big thing is: I want to actually be able to *find* things later.

A few things that would make my life better:

- When I save a link, I don't want to type out what it is. I'd love it to just grab the title and a little description and the site's icon automatically, so my list is readable at a glance instead of a wall of raw web addresses.
- I want to search across everything I've saved and actually get the right result — searching by words, not just remembering which folder I dropped it in.
- I want to label things my own way and then pull up just the links with a certain label.
- Some things I save because I want to read them later, and I'd like to keep those separate from the pile I've already dealt with.
- And I get nervous that pages disappear or change — I'd feel better knowing what I saved is still there in some form even if the original goes away.

That's the heart of it: save it fast, find it later, and trust it'll still be there. Does that give you enough to start with?

Open the [read-later prototype](http://maker:4001/index.html?flow=read-later). Check **Read later**, select **Save link**, then open **Read later** in the sidebar. Tell me how that flow feels.

This version assumes you decide a link is for later before saving it, and that those bookmarks remain in the main library while also appearing in a separate read-later view.

This feels good — checking "Read later" before saving set the link aside, and I could see it living in both places: still in my main library and also gathered in the separate Read later view in the sidebar. Keeping it in both spots is right; I wouldn't want setting something aside to make it vanish from my main collection.

Two things come to mind that are really the other half of this same idea, though:

First and most important — once I've actually read one of these, I need a way to mark it as done so it drops out of the Read later list. Otherwise that list just grows forever and stops meaning "still to read." The whole point of the list is that it empties as I get through things, so clicking something to say "I've read this" and having it leave the read-later view is essential for me.

Second, smaller: I don't always know at the moment I save something that it's for later. Often I save it normally and *then* decide I want to come back to it. So I'd want to be able to move an already-saved bookmark into Read later after the fact, not only decide it right at save time.

The setting-aside and the two-places part you've shown is exactly right — could we round it out with marking things as read to clear them, and being able to set something aside after it's already saved?
